RISKS
Workforce restructuring charges of approximately $150 million in the first quarter of 2026 due to simplification initiatives and continued rationalization of authorized retail.
Network optimization costs of approximately $450 million, mainly in the first and second quarters, due to the transition and integration of acquired assets such as U.S. Cellular, as directly detailed in the call.

SUMMARY
Management confirmed an industry-leading service revenue growth rate, driven by substantial gains in postpaid net accounts, ARPA expansion, and premium plan adoption, with explicit targets of $80.5 billion-$81.5 billion in service revenue by 2027. Strategic investments in AI-driven customer experience, most notably through TLife, Intense CX, and core network integration, are forecast to generate approximately $3 billion in incremental efficiencies and cost savings by 2027. M&A—including Metronet and U.S. Cellular—are explicitly incorporated into guidance, with nearly $8 billion in reported service revenue growth attributed to these integrations over 2026-2027. The commitment to a $52 billion capital returns envelope is underscored by an accelerated first quarter 2026 buyback of up to $5 billion, while
Deutsche Telekom
(OTC: DTEGY) will retain its stake and explore deeper investment options in T-Mobile US. The company is shifting all primary disclosure and internal incentives to postpaid account metrics and ARPA, which management asserts delivers a clearer view of customer relationship value and aligns with changes in consumer behavior. Guidance includes $10 billion in CapEx for 2026, a continued network optimization charge, and forecast margin expansion, with postpaid ARPA expected to rise 2.5%-3% annually even as normalized churn resumes across the sector.
Management stated, “we'll no longer be reporting subscriber level elements,” confirming an end to detailed phone line disclosures and focusing solely on accounts and ARPA.
New product investment is highlighted by the launch of the T-Mobile Visa credit card (in partnership with
Capital One
(NYSE: COF)) and integration of financial services, with related financial contribution excluded from core guidance.
Management expects FWA customers to reach 15 million and fiber broadband customers to reach three-four million by 2030, projecting total broadband customers of 18-19 million—all classified as incremental, not cannibalizing legacy revenue streams.
The presentation introduced “AI Live Translate”—the world’s first scale use case of AI integrated at the network core—which requires only one T-Mobile US participant and no app.
Leadership highlighted a planned industry shift away from prioritizing phone subsidies, with stated intent to focus on “win-win economics” for both customers and investors, and implied future product and pricing moves.
T-Mobile US attributed its operating leverage gains to a unique network asset strategy emphasizing customer-driven coverage, proprietary AI for CapEx allocation, and a strong culture of customer experience enforced at all touchpoints, including an in-sourced retail model.
Strategic capital deployment remains guided by a consistent leverage target of 2.5x, with excess capacity available for further shareholder returns or M&A as opportunities arise.
Direct-to-device satellite service (with Starlink) was described as a complementary product serving 500,000 square miles of uncovered territory; management insisted this offering will not compete directly with dense urban network usage.
“Account-based churn” will replace line-level churn reporting, with leadership asserting that account churn more directly represents customer value loss and reflects CLV impact.
AI RAN and edge/physical AI initiatives are expected to drive long-term industry change, but management confirmed that no meaningful upside from these new businesses is included in the 2026-2027 guidance ranges.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
ARPA
: Average Revenue Per Account, a metric reflecting total revenue generated per customer account each month.
FWA (Fixed Wireless Access)
: Broadband delivered wirelessly using the mobile network rather than fixed lines; T-Mobile US positions this as a growth segment.
TLife
: T-Mobile US’s proprietary customer application, highlighted as a central platform for engagement, self-service, and digital sales.
Intense CX
: T-Mobile US’s AI-driven customer experience initiative, developed in collaboration with OpenAI, focused on personalizing interactions and improving efficiency.
AI RAN
: Artificial Intelligence-enabled Radio Access Network, integrating AI compute with wireless radio infrastructure, referenced as a future technological differentiator.
JVs
: Joint Ventures; T-Mobile US participates in broadband expansion through JVs like MetroNet, Lumos, Bliss, and Vistar.
CDC (Customer-Driven Coverage)
: Data- and AI-guided network investment strategy that allocates CapEx to optimize customer experience rather than maximize coverage by population ("POPs").
